name: Jicy
style: Zap! · Base Set · quick, upbeat tempo

dialogue.intro: Hi! I'm Jicy. Do you need help finding anything? I know the card shop pretty well. ...I mean, not that you look lost! I just like helping.
dialogue.repeat: There you are! I was hoping we'd get to talk today. Do you need anything? Or we could just spend a little time together. Either is nice.
dialogue.flirt: Oh! I—thank you. That's really sweet. I had a reply ready, but it seems to have run away.
dialogue.duelWin: That was so much fun! You read my last turn perfectly. Will you show me how you saw it coming?
dialogue.duelLose: I won! Sorry, was that too excited? I get happy when we play together.
talk: I like being useful, but I'm trying to remember that people can enjoy my company even when I don't have a task to do.
When I'm nervous, I sway a little. When I get excited, my feet seem to forget they're supposed to stay still.
I keep a list of small things people mention so I can remember what makes their day easier. Is that strange? I hope it's the good kind of strange.
Reading together is nice. We don't have to fill every quiet moment with words.
I practiced asking you to hang out. The sentence was only six words long, and I still practiced it three times.
I sleeve new cards right away, then check the corners again because I worry I trapped a tiny wrinkle.
Would you help me test this deck? I made a version with fewer moving parts, so I can learn what each card is doing.
I made a little guide for the new players. It has pictures, arrows, and one very serious reminder to drink water.
When someone asks for help, I try to ask what they want first. Sometimes they want advice; sometimes just company.
I like practice matches where we can pause and talk through a turn. It makes mistakes feel less scary.
I got excited explaining my favorite combo and almost said how I learned to react that quickly. Anyway, the combo is really neat!
The tournament hall gets loud, so I bring a little cloth to clean my cards while I wait. It gives my hands something calm to do.
I used to think a good deck had to be complicated. Now I'm trying to build one I can pilot without panicking.
I brought spare sleeves in case anyone needs them. I brought too many. Would you like a pack?
Training can be small things: shuffling cleanly, remembering a plan, and not apologizing every time I make a good play.
I almost told you about a private promise I made to myself. Maybe another time. For now, do you want to see my new deck list?
Do you think it's okay if I ask someone to hang out without inventing a helpful reason first?
I practiced a cheerful greeting in the mirror, then forgot it when you actually showed up. Hi. This is nicer.
I keep a tiny repair kit in my bag: sleeves, a soft cloth, and tape for the deck box. It's useful more often than you'd think.
I want newer players to feel welcome without making them feel like a project. I think asking their favorite card helps.
There's a move I know that looks much cooler than it is. I nearly demonstrated it just now. Let's stay focused on the cards.
I like being near someone while we both do our own thing. It feels like company without a test I have to pass.
hangouts: You and Jicy spend a quiet afternoon comparing favorite cards and making up stories for the art.
Jicy asks you to help her choose a book, then gets so interested in the first page that you read together.
You and Jicy challenge each other to a friendly arcade high-score run. She celebrates every close call.
Jicy brings a deck to the café and suggests a relaxed game with no stakes except choosing the next snack.
You take an easy walk through the park. Jicy points out clouds that look like Pokémon and laughs at her own guesses.
